question: Give the name of the league with the highest matches of all time and how many matches were played in the said league.
evidence: league with highest matches of all time refers to MAX(COUNT(league_id));
clarification: Also keep rows that have no matching the joined table record.
gold: SELECT t2.name, t1.max_count FROM League AS t2 LEFT JOIN (SELECT league_id, MAX(cnt) AS max_count FROM (SELECT league_id, COUNT(id) AS cnt FROM Match GROUP BY league_id) AS subquery) AS t1 ON t1.league_id = t2.id
gold0: SELECT t2.name, t1.max_count FROM League AS t2 JOIN (SELECT league_id, MAX(cnt) AS max_count FROM (SELECT league_id, COUNT(id) AS cnt FROM Match GROUP BY league_id) AS subquery) AS t1 ON t1.league_id = t2.id

d.request: Which league has the most matches of all time (the maximum count of matches per league_id), and how many matches were played in it, when the join between leagues and matches also keeps league rows that have no matching match records (i.e., using a left join so unmatched rows are retained)?
d.sql: SELECT L.id AS league_id, L.name, COUNT(M.id) AS match_count FROM League L LEFT JOIN Match M ON L.id = M.league_id GROUP BY L.id, L.name ORDER BY match_count DESC LIMIT 1

b.request: Using a left join from League to Match so leagues with no matches are kept (counted as zero), find the league name with the highest match count and that count
b.sql: SELECT L.name, COUNT(M.id) AS match_count FROM League L LEFT JOIN Match M ON M.league_id = L.id GROUP BY L.id, L.name ORDER BY match_count DESC LIMIT 1

c.sql: SELECT L.name, COUNT(M.league_id) AS match_count FROM Match M LEFT JOIN League L ON M.league_id = L.id GROUP BY M.league_id ORDER BY match_count DESC LIMIT 1
